import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Fill NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' with 'None' for clearer categorization
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Create a custom color palette for the different sleep disorders for visual clarity
disorder_palette = {
    'None': '#1f77b4',        # Muted Blue
    'Sleep Apnea': '#ff7f0e',  # Safety Orange
    'Insomnia': '#d62728'      # Brick Red
}

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create the bubble chart using seaborn's scatterplot
# x-axis: Physical Activity Level
# y-axis: Sleep Duration
# hue: Sleep Disorder (color of the bubbles)
# size: Stress Level (size of the bubbles)
# style: BMI Category (shape of the markers)
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Physical Activity Level',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level',
    style='BMI Category',
    palette=disorder_palette,
    sizes=(40, 600),  # Range of bubble sizes
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set the main title and a descriptive subtitle
fig.suptitle(
    'The Relationship Between Lifestyle and Sleep',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    y=0.98
)
ax.set_title(
    'Sleep duration vs. physical activity, influenced by stress, BMI, and sleep disorders',
    fontsize=14,
    pad=20
)

# Set axis labels with units
ax.set_xlabel('Physical Activity Level (minutes/day)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Add reference lines for recommended sleep duration (7-9 hours for adults)
ax.axhspan(7, 9, color='green', alpha=0.1, zorder=0)
ax.text(
    df['Physical Activity Level'].max() + 2,
    8,
    'Recommended\nSleep Zone\n(7-9 hours)',
    verticalalignment='center',
    horizontalalignment='left',
    fontsize=10,
    color='darkgreen',
    fontstyle='italic'
)

# --- Legend Customization ---
# Improve legend clarity and position it outside the main plot
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()

# Find the starting index for each legend section
try:
    disorder_idx = labels.index('Sleep Disorder')
    stress_idx = labels.index('Stress Level')
    bmi_idx = labels.index('BMI Category')
except ValueError: # Handle cases where a section might be missing
    disorder_idx, stress_idx, bmi_idx = 0, 0, 0 # Default values
    for i, label in enumerate(labels):
        if label == 'Sleep Disorder': disorder_idx = i
        if label == 'Stress Level': stress_idx = i
        if label == 'BMI Category': bmi_idx = i


# Create a new legend for Sleep Disorder
legend1 = ax.legend(
    handles[disorder_idx+1:stress_idx],
    labels[disorder_idx+1:stress_idx],
    title='Sleep Disorder',
    title_fontsize='13',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    frameon=True,
    shadow=True
)
ax.add_artist(legend1)

# Create a new legend for Stress Level
legend2 = ax.legend(
    handles[stress_idx+1:bmi_idx],
    labels[stress_idx+1:bmi_idx],
    title='Stress Level',
    title_fontsize='13',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.70),
    loc='upper left',
    frameon=True,
    shadow=True
)
ax.add_artist(legend2)

# Create a new legend for BMI Category
legend3 = ax.legend(
    handles[bmi_idx+1:],
    labels[bmi_idx+1:],
    title='BMI Category',
    title_fontsize='13',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.40),
    loc='upper left',
    frameon=True,
    shadow=True
)

# --- Save the Figure ---
# Adjust layout to make room for the title and legend
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
